text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: GPU ECC error rate spike detected in g-cluster-7 (5m avg >= 12 errors/min). Auto-page sent to oncall.

Alex: grabbing this — oncall for this shift. seeing a cluster-level spike in ECC counts. paging history shows multiple noisy nodes.

Mira: FYI customer-facing services show elevated retry rates from generator-prod across three zones, but no 5xx. Latency up ~80ms for small requests.

Sam: can you paste the alert query? want to check if it's per-node or aggregated.

Alex: alert query from grafana:
```
sum by(instance)(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) > 10
```
we're firing on sum across the pool, which lumps noisy nodes with healthy ones.

Cheng: TL;DR: a single drifting node can blow past the sum threshold. we should avoid pool-level sum for paging.

Ryan: agree. recommendation: change to per-node threshold + sustained window and add suppression for transient bursts. e.g.
```
max by(node)(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[10m])) > 2
```
plus `for: 15m` on the alert rule.

Mira: that would reduce noise. also recommend adding a tag to include node role (inference vs infra) so we don't page on infra-only nodes during low-impact windows.

Alex: checking node list now. found node g-node-7b with ECC rate ~45/min. others mostly <1. looks like a single hot node.

Sam: can we isolate it? drain? how will that impact customer traffic? generator-prod has multi-replica, should be fine but want canary drain steps.

Alex: plan: 1) mark node as degraded in fleet 2) drain non-critical workloads, 3) run ECC soft reset (if available) 4) monitor.

Mira: for step 3, PGPU firmware reset requires host reboot if soft reset fails. we should coordinate with SRE-runbook and send notice to customers if we expect >5m impact.

Cheng: also propose an 'ECC noisy node' dashboard tile: per-node ECC rate heatmap + VRAM pressure + GPU temp; add a sparkline for 1h trend. that'll help oncall triage quickly.

Ryan: adding dashboard panels: ECC/errors per node, vram_used_percent, temp_c, and evict_count. suggest we place it on the 'inference hardware' row.

Alex: executing drain on g-node-7b now (cordon + migrate pods). patching drain command:
```
kubectl cordon g-node-7b
kubectl drain g-node-7b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
```

ops-bot: Migration started: 17 pods rescheduled, ETA ~3m.

Mira: watching customer metrics — generator-prod latency dipping back down as pods reschedule. good sign.

Sam: what about alert tuning besides switching from sum->max? Also worried about VRAM OOM alerts that have been noisy when preemptible bursts happen.

Cheng: recommend multi-signal alert rule: require ECC AND VRAM pressure OR node thermal anomaly to page. e.g.
```
(ecc_rate_per_node > 2 AND (vram_used_percent > 92 OR temp_c > 90))
```
with 'for: 10m' to avoid transient spikes.

Alex: that would reduce pages for purely ECC microbursts that don't affect runtime. we should set a lower-severity alert for single-signal so engineers can see in dash but not get paged.

Ryan: propose severities: P0 (service degradation/customer impact) P1 (node health that may lead to P0) P2 (informational). ECC-only -> P2, ECC+vram/thermals -> P1.

Mira: capture customer impact in the incident doc: generator-prod increased retries; estimated 0.7% of requests affected for 12m. I'll file a short post-incident note after we stabilize.

Alex: ops-bot: g-node-7b ECC rate dropping after drain. running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=...` shows no persistent faults. planning soft reset once eviction finished.

ops-bot: Migration complete: 0 pods left on g-node-7b.

Alex: performed ECC soft reset via admin tool — telemetry shows errors reduced to baseline. marking node as schedulable in 30m pending stable telemetry.

Sam: can we add a short playbook entry for this pattern: 'single noisy GPU node -> cordon+drain -> soft reset -> observe 30m -> uncordon'? saves time on future pages.

Cheng: I'll draft the playbook and the dashboard PR. also will open an alert-rule PR to replace pool-sum with per-node rule + composite rule for paging severity. want reviewers: Alex, Mira, Ryan.

Mira: ack. include a note in PR about rationale and the customer impact brief.

Alex: handoff to night oncall @Koh in 20m. current status: node stable, no further ECC spikes. generator-prod latency recovered. we will leave a P2 log entry and the alert suppression change in draft until PR merges.

Koh: thanks @Alex — I'll take it. if ECC rises again will escalate. please add runbook link.

Alex: runbook: https://internal/gpu-runbooks/noisy-ecc-node

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident summary recorded. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Ticket: INC-2026.

Mira: small note — please queue a scheduled check for that node's firmware next maintenance window. likely recurrence if hardware marginal.

Alex: thanks team. closing the page. :white_check_mark:
